title: CLCON/10/2009 of SMT MANORAMA KAINTORA Vs S.P.KHALI and ANOTHER

paras.text:
HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND, AT NAINITAL
Civil Contempt Petition No.10 of 2009
Smt. Manorama Kaintora
W/o Shri Vijai Singh Kaintora ... Petitioner
Versus
Sri S. P. Khali,
Addl. District Basic Education
Officer & another ... Respondents
Dated:- 22nd February, 2010
Hon'ble Tarun Agarwala, J.
 Heard Ms. Jyoti Joshi, Advocate holding brief of Mr. B. D.
Upadhyaya, the learned counsel for the petitioner and Mr. J. P.
Joshi, the learned Chief Standing Counsel for the State of
Uttarakhand.
Pursuant to the order of this Court dated 18th February, 2010, Mr. J.
P. Joshi, the learned Chief Standing Counsel has placed a demand
draft No.333151 dated 20th February, 2010 issued by the State Bank
of India, Pauri Branch in favour of the applicant Smt. Manorama
Kaintura for a sum of Rs.1,33,189/- towards the payment of interest
in compliance of the order of writ court dated 28th July, 2004.
It has taken five and a half years for the opposite party to comply
with the order of the writ court. The opposite party should not be
proud of this fact and should be ashamed. The Court, inspite of the
compliance of the orders of the writ court, can still haul up the
opposite party and sue them for contempt proceedings. Since, the
contempt is writ large, but in the circumstances of the case, the
Court has also to see that the order of the writ court is complied with
instead of pursuing the matter.
Since the arrears had already been paid earlier and now the interest
portion is being paid through a demand draft, the Court is of the
opinion that substantial compliance of the order of the writ court has
now been made and that no useful purpose would be served in
keeping these proceedings pending any further.
Accordingly, this Court directs the Reader of this Court to take a
photocopy of the demand draft and keep it on record and handover
the original demand draft to Ms. Jyoti Joshi, Advocate holding brief
of Mr. B. D. Upadhyaya, the learned counsel for the applicant, who
in turn will handover the same to the applicant. An endorsement
from the learned counsel about the receipt of the demand draft shall
be taken by the Reader on the order sheet.
In view of the aforesaid, notices are discharged and contempt
petition is dismissed.
 (Tarun Agarwala, J.)
